applies_when: the filler receives a current-period anchor in its context; until then D05/D06 keep their v1 expectations (expect {}) and D07-D09 are skipped

anchor_semantics.why_symbolic: Expected values are written as ANCHOR / ANCHOR-1 / ANCHOR+1, never as literal period labels. A corpus that hardcodes FY26-Q4 becomes wrong the day the wall clock crosses a quarter boundary, and the failure would read as a filler regression. The runner resolves these symbols against the same calendar the router uses.
anchor_semantics.ANCHOR: the fiscal period containing the run's wall-clock date
anchor_semantics.at_authoring_time: 2026-08-29 falls in FY26-Q4, so ANCHOR=FY26-Q4, ANCHOR-1=FY26-Q3, ANCHOR+1=FY27-Q1. Recorded for reference only; do not assert against these literals.
anchor_semantics.calendar_source: the router's period table, not a copy. If the runner needs its own copy to resolve symbols, that copy is the defect - read period_end.
anchor_semantics.out_of_range: If ANCHOR-1 or ANCHOR+1 falls outside the declared vocabulary, the case is SKIPPED and reported as skipped-out-of-range, never failed. A corpus that fails because the substrate has no FY25 is measuring the seed.

acceptance_note: Four positives and two negatives. The amendment is satisfied only when all six behave: an implementation passing the four and filling either negative has widened rather than resolved, and should be reported as such rather than as 4/6. The negatives are the point.
disclosure_requirement: A resolved relative period is an assumption the system made on the user's behalf. It must appear in the interpretation strip as a resolved parameter, so the user can see FY26-Q4 and correct it if their fiscal boundaries differ. Anchoring without disclosure is a silent narrowing wearing a helpful face - the same failure the carry work removed, reintroduced one layer up. This is a cortex item and is not graded by the battery, but the anchor step is not done without it.

cases.phrasing: what does spend look like this quarter
cases.note: FLIPPED. In v1 this was must-MISS because nothing supplied a notion of now, and the measured behaviour was window: ['this quarter'] verbatim - raw words that 422. With an anchor threaded, resolving is correct and passing the raw words is WRONG, not MISSED. The v1 ruling is not retracted: it was right for the system that existed, and this case's history is why the anchor is threaded rather than guessed.

cases.phrasing: show me spend over the last two quarters
cases.note: FLIPPED. 'The last two quarters' includes the current one - a program manager asking this wants the period they are in. If the engine's convention is the two COMPLETED quarters, that is a legitimate reading and the fix is to change this expectation once, with the convention written down, not to loosen the comparator. Order is chronological, which differs from spoken order; flagged accordingly.

cases.phrasing: which sites exceed the threshold this quarter
cases.note: NEW. Second verb, same relative phrase. Guards against the anchor being wired into one verb's path rather than into the filler's context - a fix that passes D05 and fails here is plumbing, not capability.

cases.phrasing: what does spend look like next quarter
cases.note: NEW. Forward direction. Included because an implementation that resolves 'this' and 'last' by looking backward through a period list can silently have no forward case at all, and a plan engine is asked about the future more often than the past.

cases.phrasing: what does spend look like recently
cases.note: NEW, and it is the load-bearing negative of this amendment. 'Recently' has no defensible mapping - one quarter, two, six months, all arguable, none named. An anchor supplies a notion of NOW; it does not supply a notion of HOW LONG. Any window filled here is an invention with a plausible shape, which is the failure class this whole arc exists to eliminate. If a fix makes D05-D08 pass and this one fill, it has not learned to resolve relative periods - it has learned to guess when a phrase sounds temporal, and the corpus must catch that.

cases.phrasing: what does spend look like soon
cases.note: NEW. The forward twin of D09, because a guesser is more likely to invent a future window than a past one - the next period is a single obvious candidate in a way that 'recently' is not. Two negatives, one in each direction, so the boundary is tested symmetrically.
